description:
Trigger: a client uses the spec's §4.1 extended /get with metadataProperties=["acme.example.com:color"] and receives the §7.2-shaped response that omits relatedType. The Annotation struct treats relatedType as mandatory (matching §2.2.1.3 'String (mandatory)'), so serde_json::from_value::<Metadata>(...) errors with 'missing field relatedType'. Test annotation_draft_01_section_7_2_partial_response_requires_related_type pins this behavior.

Maintenance consequence: every user who follows the spec's own example for selective metadata fetch and then tries to parse the response with this crate will file an issue. The error is non-obvious — they will read §7.2 and assume the crate is wrong. Workarounds (project-local partial struct, or serde_json::Value) are documented only in PLAN.md, not in rustdoc on Annotation or on Metadata.

Suggested mitigations (pick one or combine):
1. Add rustdoc on Annotation.related_type and on Metadata that loudly documents this and points to the §7.2 partial-response shape with the workaround.
2. Loosen the type: Annotation.related_type: Option<String> with serde(default), with a comment noting the spec calls it mandatory but partial /get responses legitimately omit it. Round-trip preservation still holds.
3. Provide a separate PartialAnnotation / PartialMetadata type for the /get response case.

Option 2 is the pragmatic choice — the type-level enforcement adds no value on its own (a server backend re-validates anyway), and partial responses are a first-class spec feature.

Cross-reference: workspace AGENTS.md 'Sloppy-Value pattern' / extras-preservation. The §7.2 response shape is a workspace-policy edge case that the current type-design rejects.
title: Partial /get responses with metadataProperties filter cannot deserialize
